title: Partition into K Equal-Sum Subsets
hints: first check the easy rejections: if the total sum isn't divisible by k, or if any single element exceeds sum/k, there's no way to succeed
the target sum for every group is total_sum / k - now the problem is 'can I repeatedly carve out groups of exactly this sum from the remaining unused elements, k times?'

recurse by building one group at a time: try adding each unused element to the current group's running sum, and if it doesn't exceed the target, mark it used and recurse to keep filling that same group

when a group's running sum hits the target exactly, start a fresh group (reset running sum to 0) and recurse again; you're done once k groups have been completed - and if a branch dead-ends, unmark the element you tried (undo) before trying a different one
commonMistakes: not pruning when a single element already exceeds the target group sum, wasting time on impossible branches
not skipping equal-valued elements that already failed at the same decision point, causing redundant repeated work (a big performance issue even if not a correctness one)
forgetting to check total_sum % k != 0 up front, missing an easy early rejection

content.problemStatement:
You're given a list of positive integers `nums` and an integer `k`.

**Determine whether the list can be split into k non-empty groups, using every element exactly once, such that every group's elements sum to the same value.**
constraints: all values in nums are positive integers
every group must be non-empty and every element must be used exactly once, in exactly one group
notes: the total sum is not evenly divisible by k (always false)
k equals the length of nums (every element must be its own group, so all values must already be equal)
an element larger than the target group sum on its own (always false)

optimal.time: O(k^n) worst case, but pruning target-sum overflow and using a visited/used array cuts the practical search drastically
optimal.space: O(n) for the used-elements tracking and recursion depth
optimal.pattern: backtracking that fills one group completely (up to the shared target sum) before starting the next, undoing an element's assignment when a group can't be completed

bruteForce.approach: try every way to assign each element to one of k labeled groups (k^n assignments) and check whether all k group sums are equal
